items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: And I had an Art Tatum trio record which my mother bought for me

ctx.x: So you came to the instrument at least kind of late in comparison to some people. Did you come to the music late though or was that always—

Well no. I had Art Hodes’ records when I was five years old. My older brother and Bob Hodes, Art’s son, were in first grade together in West Hempstead Long Island. We lived there for a very brief period of time when I was like three, four and five. So my father and Art Hodes, and my mother and Art and Thelma Hodes they all became friends. And so I had these 78s. I have a few of them left. “Way Down Yonder in New Orleans” is on one side and a tune called “Save It Pretty Mama” is on the other side. I can’t believe…
